facts.text: DC magnetron-sputtered AlTiCrZrNbTa coatings near 4 μm thick were varied across nominal Al contents of 0, 5, 10, 17, and 25 at.%.
The measured Al contents of the five coatings were 0, 6.46, 11.16, 17.43, and 25.4 at.%.
All coating compositions were oxidized isothermally at 1000 °C for 60 min in flowing steam generated from ultrapure water supplied at 0.2 mL/min.
The Al-10 coating was additionally oxidized in steam at 1100 °C for 30 min.
Post-oxidation indentation was performed using a 0.98 N load and a 15 s dwell.
Oxidation of the Al-10 coating formed a dense, continuous, adherent Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3-rich surface layer that limited oxygen diffusion into the residual coating and substrate.
At Al contents of at least 17 at.%, Al-Ti and Al-Zr intermetallic formation restricted Ti/Cr surface enrichment and promoted discontinuity of the protective oxide layer.
At 1000 °C for 60 min, Al-10 had the lowest oxidation mass gain, negligible oxygen penetration into Zry-4, and less cracking or delamination than Al-0, Al-5, Al-17, and Al-25.
The parabolic oxidation-rate constants at 1000 °C were approximately 13.1, 10, 1.2, 3.5, and 25.9 mg^2 cm^-4 min^-1 for Al-0, Al-5, Al-10, Al-17, and Al-25, respectively.
Increasing Al to nominally 17 or 25 at.% reversed the protection seen for Al-10 and allowed substantial or complete oxidation of the Zry-4 substrate.
Al-10 remained an effective oxygen barrier after oxidation at 1100 °C for 30 min in steam.
The authors identified an effective Al range of approximately 9–14 at.% for these coatings under the tested steam-oxidation conditions.
